thread:
maya: Customer report - acme-prod hitting 429s during a traffic spike. Dedicated pool dp-72 didn't scale past min_replicas=2 even though CPU/token demand high. Started ~09:12 UTC.
raj: can you paste a couple request ids + which route they hit?
maya: route: /v1/dedicated/predict, req ids: r-3a9f, r-3aa0, r-3aa4. sample log snippet: 
[09:13:45] ERROR attach-controller: failed attach for pod acme-prod-req r-3a9f: ImagePullBackOff registry.redwood.io rate limited
kevin: quick glance — looks like warm-pool attach was blocked. If attach controller is stuck, new warm pods don't join and autoscaler stays at min. Any auth errors too?
maya: yes, saw repeated 401s around same time: 
ERROR iam: GetToken failed status=401 serviceAccount=node-pool-sa account=acme-prod
sophie: customer confirms min=2 max=10 and they had a sudden 6x spike. We should've opened more.
ops-bot: autoscaler.event: probe_failure_count=6 probe_backoff=120s last_probe=2026-03-16T09:14:10Z current_replicas=2 desired_replicas=8 reason="attach-unready"
raj: repro steps I ran in staging to mimic: 
```
# barrage traffic to dedicated route
ab -n 300 -c 60 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://dedicated.example/v1/predict"
```
kevin: reproduced locally — attach-controller hit registry 429s and IAM rotations overlapped with token refresh which returned 401 intermittently. Attachment handshake times out -> pod unready -> autoscaler probe suppression. Noisy neighbor on registry caused spike.
maya: customer timeline: 09:11 normal, 09:12 spike, 09:12-09:20 repeated 429s and slow responses, some 502s, majority 429.
raj: immediate mitigations we tried: 1) bumped warm_pool_prewarm for acme-prod from 2->5, 2) temporarily increased max_burst to allow more ephemeral capacity, 3) restarted attach-controller for that account.
sophie: after changes traffic improved but still saw transient 429s for ~3 minutes while pool filled. Customer reported fewer errors after 09:25.
kevin: long-term actions: - add backoff-aware attach retries when registry returns 429 - surface registry quota metrics to customer console - decouple IAM rotation from attach hot-path to avoid 401 race - consider probe tuning to tolerate short attach windows
maya: collected artifacts: kube events, attach-controller logs, registry 429 traces, IAM rotation timestamps. Pushing to ticket RDW-3245.
raj: can ops check if any other tenants hit similar registry bursts at that window? Could be noisy neighbor from partner deploys.
kevin: also add a canary that simulates imagepull at scale to catch regressions.
ops-bot: ticket RDW-3245 created and assigned: eng-platform (kevin), oncall (raj), account (sophie).
maya: customer escalated to sev2 during peak, informed them root cause hypothesis and mitigations. They're OK with follow-ups. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
